title: LLM Reading Tea Leaves: Automatically Evaluating Topic Models with Large Language Models
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 13
subcategory: joint LLM-based evaluation of topics and document representations
task: Evaluating topic models jointly on topics and document representations
problem: Existing metrics evaluate topics (e.g. NPMI) or document representations (e.g. classification) separately and these often disagree; perplexity is not comparable across model types.
architecture: WALM: for each document, the topic model's document-word distribution (inference + generation) gives its top-10 'topical words'; an LLM (Llama-3-8B-Instruct, greedy decoding) generates keywords for the same document (plain or topic-aware prompting); agreement measured with overlap-based (exact, synset) and embedding-based (GloVe, optimal-assignment, optimal-transport) metrics.
key_results: WALM correlates only weakly with perplexity and moderately with document-representation metrics, so it adds a separate view.
Human keywords from three annotators on 200 test documents were used to measure the gap between LLM-based and human-based WALM scores.
strengths: One metric that covers both topics and document representations and works across model types.

limitations.text: Optimising for WALM alone may inherit LLM biases; should be used with other metrics.
Two datasets and one main LLM; human validation on 200 documents with one model (NVDM, K = 50).
